scenario: A btrfs mount whose device basename is listed under two different uuids under /sys/fs/btrfs, so the device-to-filesystem mapping is ambiguous and the quota state is unknown rather than enabled or disabled.

fixture.mountinfo:
23 28 0:21 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:12 - proc proc rw
24 1 0:30 /@root / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/dm-0 rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=256,subvol=/@root
30 28 259:1 / /tmp rw,relatime shared:1 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,noquota
36 28 0:44 /@data /srv/data rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/dm-3 rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@data

rationale: Contract section C2, quota-classification table, the three btrfs rows: (a) 'source basename maps to exactly one uuid whose qgroups is true' -> enabled / unknown / btrfs_qgroups_dir_present; (b) '... exactly one uuid, qgroups false' -> disabled / n/a / btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent; (c) 'zero or several uuids list the device' -> unknown / n/a / btrfs_device_unmapped. This fixture places the device basename dm-3 in the devices list of TWO uuids (a7c3e9d1-4f62-4b8e-9d21-5c7f0a3b6e11 and f2b5d804-7c19-4e62-8a3d-91b0e5c7d2a4), so rows (a) and (b) do not apply -- neither is conditioned on the mapping reaching exactly one uuid -- and row (c) governs: quota_state unknown, enforcement n/a, basis btrfs_device_unmapped. The two claimants deliberately AGREE on qgroups (both true, mode 'qgroup') so that the expectation 'unknown' holds under every reading of rows (a) and (b): no reading of 'exactly one uuid whose qgroups is true' is satisfied by two claimants, and no reading of 'exactly one uuid, qgroups false' is satisfied either. The case therefore isolates the row (c) condition alone, and an implementation that resolves the device by taking the first, the last, or any single matching uuid, or that resolves it by the raw source basename instead of the device_links map, lands on 'enabled' and is caught. Mount resolution follows the contract rule 'candidate mounts: mount point equals realpath, or is /, or realpath starts with mount point + /; choose the longest mount point; among equal mount points the last line wins' read over the proc.rst section 3.5 field layout (S082, Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst:1965-1990: fields 1-6, optional fields until the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source, super options): for realpath /srv/data/store the candidates are '/' (the /@root btrfs line) and '/srv/data' (the /@data btrfs line, since /srv/data/store starts with '/srv/data/'); the longest wins, so mount_point is /srv/data, fstype btrfs, mount source /dev/dm-3, and the '/' candidate is not selected. Device check: fstype is btrfs and the mount major:minor 0:44 differs from the path st_dev 0:57, so the non-btrfs device_mismatch verdict does not apply; per S081 (fs/btrfs/inode.c, btrfs_getattr:8215-8218 and 'stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev' at 8246) a btrfs path reports the subvolume's anonymous device number, so the mismatch is expected and is recorded as device_check btrfs_subvolume_skipped, and the path proceeds to quota classification. The frozen real control frozen/c2-expected-real.json corroborates this reading: its btrfs fleet root (mount 0:30, st_dev 0:57) carries basis btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent, not device_mismatch. S079 (fs/btrfs/sysfs.c) supports the fixture's device-mapping shape: the per-fsid 'devices' kobject is created under /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/devices (fs_devs->devices_kobj = kobject_create_and_add("devices", ...), sysfs.c:2266) and btrfs_sysfs_add_device links each block device into it by the block device's own kernel name (sysfs_create_link(devices_kobj, disk_kobj, disk_kobj->name), sysfs.c:2155), which is the name the contract calls the device basename; the same file shows the 'qgroups' group under /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/qgroups/ with its 'enabled' and 'mode' attributes (qgroup_enabled_show at 2355, qgroup_mode_show at 2370, the qgroups attribute group and its path comment at 2450-2461) that the fixture's qgroups / qgroups_mode fields mirror, and qgroup_mode_show emits exactly 'qgroup' (BTRFS_QGROUP_MODE_FULL) or 'squota' (BTRFS_QGROUP_MODE_SIMPLE), so 'qgroup' is a legal mode text. S080 (fs/btrfs/qgroup.c) supports the meaning of the qgroups flag: btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups creates that group when qgroups are initialised (qgroup.c:441 and :1032) and btrfs_sysfs_del_qgroups destroys it (qgroup.c:620, :689, :1295), so qgroups false means the group is absent for that filesystem and qgroups true means it is present. Verdict precedence: the fixture is well formed (no setup error), no path is enabled, the single path is unknown, therefore exit 2 and finding_id QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN.
